dual_block_characterization.watchdog_header: 11-02 17:35:48.818 4064 4156 W Watchdog: *** WATCHDOG KILLING SYSTEM PROCESS: Blocked in handler on on foreground thread (android.fg) for 60s, Blocked in handler on on main thread (main) for 60s

main_thread_half.name: main
main_thread_half.mechanism: Pre-created /data/vendor_de/0/fpdata (0700 1000:1000) and early direct-spawned /vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint-service.ranchu from t636-diag.sh prep with supervision. IFingerprint/default registered early with servicemanager (lines 4204, 4619). FingerprintProvider.getHalInstance() acquired the HAL cleanly without blocking on main thread.

android_fg_half.name: android.fg
android_fg_half.mechanism: OverlayManagerService closed its connection to idmap2d after user 0 overlay verification. Connection.close() posted IdmapDaemon.stopIdmapService() to android.fg, calling SystemService.stop('idmap2d') -> SystemProperties.set('ctl.stop', 'idmap2d'). Because init processes only 1 control message per main loop iteration and the control message queue was saturated with dropped messages due to hwservicemanager repeatedly polling missing android.hardware.media.c2@1.0::IComponentStore/software (lines 37718-41268), android.fg blocked inside __system_property_set waiting on /dev/socket/property_service for init to reply, leading to Watchdog killing system_server PID 3765 at line 42754.
android_fg_half.ruling_out_evidence: In Flight-01, the main thread was completely unblocked (0s), yet android.fg still blocked for 94s. This disproved the hypothesis that android.fg was merely a co-present symptom of main-thread lazy HAL waiting. The init property socket / control queue congestion is independently sustained by hwservicemanager media.c2 flooding.
